newsitem.title: USA: USDA fixing emergency feed program, senator says.
newsitem.headline: USDA fixing emergency feed program, senator says.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman made changes to an emergency livestock feeding programme late on Friday and assured lawmakers he would do all he could to help farmers, said senator Byron Dorgan.

Dorgan said Glickman agreed to explore the possibility of extending the programme to get emergency feed to livestock affected by severe winter storms in portions of the Midwest and would accept applications for assistance under the programme later than the previously announced deadline of Jan. 25.
Dorgan said USDA also said a longer term 30-percent federal cost share programme for emergency feed would go forward, despite an earlier decision to halt it.
Dorgan and Sen. Tom Daschle, D-S.Dakota, had sharply criticized USDA's response to the winter emergency, saying it didn't provide the help that was needed.

Both senators on Friday praised Glickman's actions and said the secretary assured them he would "move as aggressively as he can to respond to what he knows is a severe winter emergency for livestock, farmers and ranchers in the Dakotas," Dorgan said.
Tens of thousands of cattle have already perished in the storms.
